modelspec.checkpoint.DType.title: DType
modelspec.checkpoint.DType.description: A tensor element type and its size in bytes; `f32` for every value, `i32` only for row ids an `embedding` reads, never a parameter or a checkpoint tensor (DESIGN.md § 2.2).

modelspec.checkpoint.Shape.title: Shape
modelspec.checkpoint.Shape.description: A tensor shape; each dimension is a positive integer and rank 0 is a scalar (DESIGN.md § 2.2).

modelspec.diagram.GlyphId.title: GlyphId
modelspec.diagram.GlyphId.description: The id of one SVG symbol of the glyph set (DESIGN.md § 13.1). `op-<operator>` for each Tensor IR operation, the operator in kebab case (`op-mat-mul`, `op-layer-norm-grad-x`), an Input also `op-input-token` for a dropout RNG token and `op-input-step` for a host input of an AdamW step; `scope-<kind>` for a composite of a Function, Adjoint, Module or Layer scope and `scope-update-<optimizer>` for an Update scope; `stage-<stage>` for a pipeline stage; `endpoint-<role>` for an endpoint. Every TensorOp variant has exactly one, and a gradient op's glyph is its forward operator's with the gradient mark.

modelspec.diagram.PipelineStage.title: PipelineStage
modelspec.diagram.PipelineStage.description: A stage of a pipeline view, each one composite node of the view's root (DESIGN.md § 13.4). Forward, Loss, Backward and Optimizer are the Training IR subgraphs Forward, Loss, Gradient and Optimizer; Data holds the program's Input nodes (inputs, targets, packed batch tensors, dropout RNG tokens, the host inputs of an AdamW step); Parameters holds every ParamRead at its state version. A checkpoint and a prediction are Endpoint nodes (EndpointRole), never stages.

modelspec.diagram.Port.title: Port
modelspec.diagram.Port.description: A tensor crossing a scope's boundary; a collapsed scope's composite node draws one port per entry, and an edge to or from a node inside the scope attaches to it (DESIGN.md § 13.3).

value_id.description: The value that crosses, defined outside the scope for In and inside it for Out.

modelspec.diagram.Scope.title: Scope
modelspec.diagram.Scope.description: One scope of the graph's scope tree with its boundary ports, outermost segment first.

parent.description: Absent exactly on the root, the Program scope.

stage.description: The pipeline stage the scope sits in, absent in a Model graph.

modelspec.diagram.ScopeKey.title: ScopeKey
modelspec.diagram.ScopeKey.description: The canonical text of a scope path, unique within a graph and used as the composite node's key, an anchor on the documentation site and a file name (DESIGN.md § 13.2). The segments joined by `/`; a Program segment is the train block's name; a Stage segment its lower-case name; a Function segment `<fn>` for the first inlining of the function in the program and `<fn>@<c>` for inlining c from 1, the naming of dropout sites (DESIGN.md § 2.3); an Adjoint segment `grad%<k>`, k the forward ValueId; an Update segment `update@<parameter path>`.

modelspec.diagram.ScopeKind.title: ScopeKind
modelspec.diagram.ScopeKind.description: What one segment of a scope path names (DESIGN.md § 13.2). Program is the root, the train block; Stage a PipelineStage; Function one inlining of a model function at one call site; Adjoint the gradient nodes the rule of one forward node emitted; Update the optimizer nodes of one parameter; Module and Layer are reserved for the module and layer instances of DESIGN.md § 11 iteration 3 and are emitted by no compiler before it.

modelspec.diagram.ScopeSegment.title: ScopeSegment
modelspec.diagram.ScopeSegment.description: One step of a scope path, outermost first.

name.description: The train block's name, the stage's lower-case name, the function's name, the forward value as `%<k>` or the parameter's canonical path (DESIGN.md § 2.3).

instance.description: For a Function segment, which inlining of the function in the program, from 0; 0 for every other kind.

call_site.description: For a Function segment, the source position of the call as a diagnostic prints it, `file:line:column` (DESIGN.md § 8.1); absent for every other kind.
